title: This week in India's growth story.
caption:
This week in India's growth story: 14 stories covering history, sectors and mindset.

1. She grew up in India, studied at Osmania University - and just won Harvard's highest honor for alumni.
2. He was executed at 19 for plotting an armed uprising against British rule. Bhagat Singh later carried his photo.
3. He was beaten by police for leading a protest. His death radicalized the generation that followed him.
4. 120 men held a mountain pass until their last round of ammunition ran out.
5. She grew up in a small Haryana town dreaming of flight. On this day, she left the atmosphere.
6. She'd lost her first Super Series final the year before. This time, she didn't let it slip.
7. India's Production Linked Incentive schemes promised investment, output and jobs. A new government assessment shows which of those three actually showed up.
8. Coal still powers most of India's grid. Last month, Coal India moved more of it in a single month than ever before.
9. India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart.
10. Prateep Basu spent years building satellites for ISRO. Then he started a company to point them at crop fields and flood zones instead.
11. Foreign investors had been cautious on Indian stocks for months. In November, that changed - fast.
12. He grew up in India, taught at Harvard - and just became one of Asia's top economists.
13. A year after taking Lenskart public, Peyush Bansal said one thing out loud: "What we have done is not enough."
14. A state spent a year asking to be renamed. Parliament finally said yes on this day.
